Sirach prays for mercy on the people called by the name of Yahuah (God), on Yashar'el (Israel) whom he named his firstborn. Yahusha (Jesus) says many will come from east and west and sit down with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom. The firstborn is one people, named from the beginning, and the many from east and west are that firstborn's scattered children coming to their fathers' table. The mercy Sirach asks for the firstborn is the seat Yahusha (Jesus) says they will take.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 36:12 — *Yashar'el (Israel), whom you have named your firstborn.* The firstborn's scattered children sit down with the fathers in Matthew 8:11.

apoc_text: Therefore let us lie in wait for the righteous; because he is not for our turn, and he is clean contrary to our doings: he upbraideth us with our offending the law, and objecteth to our infamy the transgressings of our education.
old_note: *Therefore let us lie in wait for the righteous; because he is not for our turn, and he is clean contrary to our doings: he upbraideth us with our offending the law, and objecteth to our infamy the transgressings of our education.* Wisdom of Solomon 2:12 names the righteous-one-as-rebuke-to-the-lawless architecture — the righteous man is hated by the lawless because his existence reproves their Torah-violations. The Hebrew library's wisdom-stream had been naming the righteous-sufferer architecture as the Isaiah 53 Suffering-Servant prophecy's wider Hebrew-library backdrop. Matthew's application of Isaiah 53:4 to the healing-ministry at Matt 8:17 walks the same architecture: the bearer-of-our-infirmities is the righteous-sufferer the wisdom-stream had named.
new_note: *Therefore let us lie in wait for the righteous; because he is not for our turn, and he is clean contrary to our doings: he upbraideth us with our offending the law, and objecteth to our infamy the transgressings of our education.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:12). *That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by Esaias the prophet, saying, Himself took our infirmities, and bare our sicknesses.* (Matthew 8:17). Wisdom of Solomon 2 is a long portrait of the righteous one hunted by the ungodly, from the lying in wait here to the shameful death they plan for him in verse 20. Isaiah painted the same man: despised, a man of sorrows, bearing our griefs and carrying our sorrows (Isaiah 53:3–4). Matthew says the healings fulfil that line; the one carrying away the sicknesses of Capernaum is the servant Isaiah saw. He is also the righteous one of Wisdom 2, and the reason the ungodly hate him is given here: his life reproves their breaking of the law. The one who bore our sicknesses was, at the same time, being watched by men who wanted him dead for being righteous.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:12 — *let us lie in wait for the righteous; because he is not for our turn.* The righteous one of Wisdom 2 is Isaiah's servant; at Matthew 8:17 he bears our sicknesses while the ungodly lie in wait for him.

apoc_text: For if the just man be the son of Yahuah (God), he will help him, and deliver him from the hand of his enemies.
old_note: *For if the just man be the son of Yahuah (God), he will help him, and deliver him from the hand of his enemies.* Wisdom 2:18 names the just-man-as-son-of-Yahuah architecture in the wisdom-stream's register — the lawless testing the just man by attempting his destruction, predicated on whether the Father will deliver his Son. Matt 8:17's Suffering-Servant credential walks the same architecture: the Servant is the just-man who is the Son of Yahuah (God), and the bearing-of-infirmities is operative across his Messianic ministry, not at the cross alone.
new_note: *For if the just man be the son of Yahuah (God), he will help him, and deliver him from the hand of his enemies.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:18). *That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by Esaias the prophet, saying, Himself took our infirmities, and bare our sicknesses.* (Matthew 8:17). The ungodly think the Father's help for his son would look like rescue from the hand of his enemies. Matthew shows what the help actually looked like: the son himself took our infirmities and bore our sicknesses, as Isaiah said he would. The just man who is the son of Yahuah (God) was not spared the suffering; he carried it, and carried it all through his ministry, not only on the last day. Deliverance came, but it came through the bearing and not around it.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:18 — *he will help him, and deliver him from the hand of his enemies.* The help came as bearing, not escape — *Himself took our infirmities, and bare our sicknesses* (Matthew 8:17).
writer_flag: Connection is thin (Wisdom's test of sonship against Matthew's Isaiah quotation); kept the old note's point that the bearing ran through the whole ministry and did not overstate it.

apoc_text: But your providence, O Father, governeth it: for you have made a way in the sea, and a safe path in the waves;
old_note: *But your providence, O Father, governeth it: for you have made a way in the sea, and a safe path in the waves.* Wisdom of Solomon 14:3 names the Father's-providence-governeth-the-sea architecture — the Father has made a way in the sea and a safe path in the waves. Matt 8:26's King-who-rebukes-the-winds-and-the-sea walks the same architecture in flesh-presence: the Voice that the wisdom-stream named as governing the sea now sleeps in a fishing-boat and then wakes to exercise the governance the wisdom-stream had named.
new_note: *But your providence, O Father, governeth it: for you have made a way in the sea, and a safe path in the waves;* (Wisdom of Solomon 14:3). *And he saith unto them, Why are ye fearful, O ye of little faith? Then he arose, and rebuked the winds and the sea; and there was a great calm.* (Matthew 8:26). The Father's providence governs the sea; he has made a way in it and a safe path in the waves. On the lake of Galilee the one who governs it was asleep in the stern of a fishing boat while the disciples thought they were dying. He woke, rebuked the winds and the sea, and there was a great calm. The voice Solomon credits with governing the waters was in the boat in flesh, and the rebuke that calmed the water was the same governance Wisdom had named, exercised from a wet deck by the one who had made the way in the sea in the first place.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 14:3 — *your providence, O Father, governeth it: for you have made a way in the sea.* The one who rebuked the winds and the sea (Matthew 8:26) is the one whose providence governs it.

apoc_text: Shewing that you can save from all danger: yes, though a man went to sea without art.
old_note: *Shewing that you can save from all danger: yes, though a man went to sea without art.* Wisdom 14:4 names the Father's save-from-all-danger architecture at the sea — even the inexperienced sailor is saved by the Father's governing providence. Matt 8:25's *Lord, save us: we perish* walks the same architecture: the disciples in the storm cry to the same Father whose providence the wisdom-stream had named as the sea's governor; the salvation they receive is the same governance's direct demonstration.
new_note: *Shewing that you can save from all danger: yes, though a man went to sea without art.* (Wisdom of Solomon 14:4). *And he saith unto them, Why are ye fearful, O ye of little faith? Then he arose, and rebuked the winds and the sea; and there was a great calm.* (Matthew 8:26). Solomon says the Father can save from all danger at sea, even a man who went out without the skill to be there. The disciples were fishermen, and the storm outdid their skill anyway; their cry was Lord, save us, we perish (Matthew 8:25). He answered by asking why they were fearful and then rebuking the wind and the water into a great calm. The saving Solomon prayed about was done in front of them, by the one in the boat, and the rebuke of their little faith is that they had the governor of the sea aboard and thought they were on their own.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 14:4 — *Shewing that you can save from all danger.* Lord, save us, we perish (Matthew 8:25) is answered by the one who can save from all danger at sea (Matthew 8:26).

apoc_text: He that keepeth the law brings offerings enough: he that takes heed to the commandment offers a peace offering.
old_note: *He that keepeth the law brings offerings enough: he that takes heed to the commandment offers a peace offering.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 35:1 names the wisdom-stream's reframing of sacrifice-substance: keeping the Torah IS bringing offerings enough; taking heed to the commandment IS offering a peace-offering. The Pharisaic-counterfeit form at Matt 9:11-13 is the inverse — categorical-classification of the publicans-and-sinners while keeping the sacrificial-credential intact. Yahusha (Jesus) cites Hosea 6:6 against precisely this counterfeit; the wisdom-stream had named the corrected substance centuries before — Torah-keeping IS the offering; mercy IS the sacrifice-substance.
new_note: *He that keepeth the law brings offerings enough: he that takes heed to the commandment offers a peace offering.* (Ecclesiasticus 35:1). *But go ye and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.* (Matthew 9:13). Sirach says the man who keeps the law has already brought offerings enough, and the one who takes heed to the commandment has offered a peace offering. That is the key to what Yahusha (Jesus) meant by I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, which he took from Hosea. He was not setting mercy against the Torah; mercy is the Torah kept, and the Pharisees who kept the altar while despising the publicans and sinners at his table had kept the smaller part and dropped the greater. The commandment kept is the offering Yahuah (God) wanted all along.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 35:1 — *He that keepeth the law brings offerings enough.* Mercy and not sacrifice (Matthew 9:13) is the commandment kept, which is the offering.

apoc_text: He that requiteth a goodturn offers fine flour; and he that gives alms sacrificeth praise.
old_note: *He that requiteth a goodturn offers fine flour; and he that gives alms sacrificeth praise.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 35:2 names the wisdom-stream's direct architecture: giving alms IS sacrificing praise. The acts-of-mercy ARE the sacrifice-substance the Tanakh-prophetic-stream has been naming since 1 Samuel 15:22. Matt 9:13's *I will have mercy, and not sacrifice* (Hosea 6:6) walks the same architecture at the kingdom-citizens level — the heart-Torah of mercy IS the sacrifice-substance the Pharisaic-counterfeit voids by external-credential-without-mercy.
new_note: *He that requiteth a goodturn offers fine flour; and he that gives alms sacrificeth praise.* (Ecclesiasticus 35:2). *But go ye and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.* (Matthew 9:13). Sirach says that to repay a good turn is to offer fine flour and to give alms is to sacrifice praise. These are the altar's own words, fine flour and the sacrifice of praise, set on ordinary acts of kindness. When Yahusha (Jesus) told the Pharisees to go and learn what I will have mercy, and not sacrifice means, Sirach had already written out the lesson. Mercy shown is sacrifice offered, and the man who gives alms has stood at the altar whether he knows it or not.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 35:2 — *he that gives alms sacrificeth praise.* Alms as sacrifice; *I will have mercy, and not sacrifice* (Matthew 9:13).

apoc_text: To depart from wickedness is a thing pleasing to Yahuah (God); and to forsake unrighteousness is a propitiation.
old_note: *To depart from wickedness is a thing pleasing to Yahuah (God); and to forsake unrighteousness is a propitiation.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 35:3 names the wisdom-stream's atonement-substance: turning-from-wickedness IS propitiation. The Pharisaic-counterfeit at Matt 9:11-13 is the categorical-credential-without-heart-turning; Yahusha (Jesus) calls Mattityahu (Matthew) and the publicans-and-sinners to *repentance* (v.13b) precisely because their turning IS the propitiation the wisdom-stream had named.
new_note: *To depart from wickedness is a thing pleasing to Yahuah (God); and to forsake unrighteousness is a propitiation.* (Ecclesiasticus 35:3). *But go ye and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.* (Matthew 9:13). Sirach says departing from wickedness pleases Yahuah (God) and forsaking unrighteousness is a propitiation; the turning itself is the atonement. Yahusha (Jesus) says he came to call sinners to repentance, not the righteous, in the same breath as I will have mercy, and not sacrifice. The publicans at his table who turned had made the offering Sirach describes; the men standing outside objecting to the company had brought their sacrifices and left the turning undone.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 35:3 — *to forsake unrighteousness is a propitiation.* The turning is the offering; Matthew 9:13 calls sinners to that repentance.

apoc_text: Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.
old_note: *Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.* Tobit 4:7 names the wisdom-stream's alms-and-mercy architecture as the heart-of-the-Torah-substance — giving alms with the eye-not-envious is the heart-Torah Hosea 6:6 names. The Pharisaic-counterfeit at Matt 9:11's indignation over the table-fellowship-with-sinners is the inverse: envy-of-the-mercy-extended-to-the-marginalized in the costume of purity-credential.
new_note: *Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.* (Tobit 4:7). *But go ye and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.* (Matthew 9:13). Give to the poor and turn your face from none, and the face of Yahuah (God) will not turn from you. That is the mercy Hosea asked for in place of sacrifice, the word Yahusha (Jesus) sends the Pharisees to go and learn. They were offended that he sat at table with sinners (9:11); Tobit had told his son not to turn his face from any poor man. Mercy toward the one in need is the heart of the Torah, and a system that keeps its credentials clean while turning its face away has lost the thing the commandment was for.
member_note: Tobit 4:7 — *neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.* The mercy Hosea asked for in place of sacrifice, which the Pharisees at the table had forgotten (Matthew 9:13).

apoc_text: For you layest up a good treasure for thyself against the day of necessity.
old_note: *For you layest up a good treasure for thyself against the day of necessity.* Tobit 4:9 names the alms-as-laid-up-treasure-against-the-day architecture explicitly — alms in the present-age lay up good treasure against the eschatological-day-of-necessity. The Sermon's own *lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, but lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven* (Matthew 6:19-20) walks the same architecture in the heart-Torah register; Matt 9:13's *I will have mercy, and not sacrifice* walks the same architecture at the kingdom-citizens dismantling of the Pharisaic-counterfeit.
new_note: *For you layest up a good treasure for thyself against the day of necessity.* (Tobit 4:9). *But go ye and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.* (Matthew 9:13). Alms laid up are a treasure against the day of need; Tobit sees the open hand as storing something before Yahuah (God). Yahusha (Jesus) tells the Pharisees to go learn Hosea's word, mercy and not sacrifice. They had stored up sacrifices and credentials; the heart of the Torah was the mercy Tobit's son was told to lay up. The treasure that counts in the day of necessity is the mercy that was done, and the King is calling a religious system back to it.
member_note: Tobit 4:9 — *you layest up a good treasure for thyself against the day of necessity.* The treasure laid up by mercy, the thing Hosea asked for in place of sacrifice (Matthew 9:13).

apoc_text: Because that alms do deliver from death, and suffers not to come into darkness.
old_note: *Because that alms do deliver from death, and suffers not to come into darkness.* Tobit 4:10 names the alms-as-deliverance-from-death architecture in the wisdom-stream's eschatological register. The Pharisaic-counterfeit collects sacrifice-credential while withholding the mercy-substance that Tobit names as the actual deliverance-architecture. Matt 9:13's Hosea 6:6 citation walks the same diagnostic at the kingdom-citizens level: the mercy-substance IS the deliverance-substance.
new_note: *Because that alms do deliver from death, and suffers not to come into darkness.* (Tobit 4:10). *But go ye and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.* (Matthew 9:13). Tobit says alms deliver from death, and he says it in the voice of a father who has lived it. The Pharisees at Matthew's table had their sacrifices in order and their mercy withheld, and the King sent them to Hosea: mercy, and not sacrifice. Tobit had already named mercy as the thing that delivers. A religion that keeps its offerings and loses its mercy has kept the shell and lost the life.
member_note: Tobit 4:10 — *alms do deliver from death, and suffers not to come into darkness.* Mercy is what delivers, and mercy is what Hosea asked for in place of sacrifice (Matthew 9:13).

apoc_text: For alms does deliver from death, and shall purge away all sin. Those that exercise alms and righteousness shall be filled with life:
old_note: *For alms does deliver from death, and shall purge away all sin. Those that exercise alms and righteousness shall be filled with life.* Tobit 12:9 (the angel Raphael's closing instruction to Tobit and Tobias) names the alms-purges-away-all-sin architecture explicitly — the wisdom-stream's naming of the mercy-substance as the very forgiveness-substance the King exercises at the paralytic's pronouncement (Matt 9:2) and the Mattityahu (Matthew) table (Matt 9:13). Alms-and-righteousness — heart-Torah — is the deliverance-architecture both passages walk.
new_note: *For alms does deliver from death, and shall purge away all sin. Those that exercise alms and righteousness shall be filled with life:* (Tobit 12:9). *But go ye and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.* (Matthew 9:13). Raphael's last word to Tobit and Tobias is that alms deliver from death and purge away all sin, and that those who do alms and righteousness are filled with life. This is mercy given the weight of life and death. In Matthew 9 the King forgives a paralytic (9:2) and sits at table with sinners, and when the Pharisees object he sends them to Hosea: mercy, and not sacrifice. Mercy is what the Torah asked for, mercy is what delivers, and the King and the angel are saying one thing.
member_note: Tobit 12:9 — *alms does deliver from death, and shall purge away all sin.* Mercy with the weight of life and death, the mercy Hosea asked for in place of sacrifice (Matthew 9:13).

apoc_text: Give to the godly man, and help not a sinner.
old_note: *Give to the godly man, and help not a sinner.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 12:4 names the wisdom-stream's discriminating-mercy stance that the Pharisaic-counterfeit-righteousness inherited and weaponized: hold-back-mercy-from-the-sinner because the sinner is categorically excluded from the wisdom-stream's mercy-flow. The framework reads Matt 9:10's *many publicans and sinners came and sat down with him* as the King's direct-reversal of the Sirach 12 stance — the categorical-exclusion the wisdom-stream had taught is dismantled at the table the King keeps.
new_note: *Give to the godly man, and help not a sinner.* (Ecclesiasticus 12:4). *And it came to pass, as Yahusha (Jesus) sat at meat in the house, behold, many publicans and sinners came and sat down with him and his disciples.* (Matthew 9:10). Sirach says to give to the godly man and not to help a sinner, and the next verse shows what he means — bread given to the ungodly becomes strength he uses against you. Yahusha (Jesus) sat at meat with publicans and sinners. These are not two stances at war. The sinners at that table had come to him, and he was calling them to repentance, not feeding them in their sin. Sirach guards the hand; the King opens the door; and the Pharisee who turned the one into a wall against persons had misread it and could not see the other.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 12:4 — *Give to the godly man, and help not a sinner.* Sirach guards the hand from strengthening the ungodly; the King's table at Matthew 9:10 calls sinners to turn.
writer_flag: Theology correction: the old note said Sirach 12 taught a wrong, categorical exclusion that the King reversed and superseded — pitting a scripture-level book against the gospel and dismissing Sirach's almsgiving counsel. The system that turned the caution into a wall around the table is what is corrected, not Sirach.

apoc_text: Do well to him that is lowly, but give not to the ungodly: hold back your bread, and give it not to him, lest he overmaster you thereby: for else you shall receive twice as much evil for all the good you shall have done to him.
old_note: *Do well to him that is lowly, but give not to the ungodly: hold back your bread, and give it not to him.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 12:5 names the wisdom-stream's explicit instruction the Pharisees of Matt 9:11 are operating under — hold-back-the-bread-from-the-ungodly. The Pharisaic *why eateth your Master with publicans and sinners?* indictment of Matt 9:11 IS the Sirach 12:5 framework operative; Yahusha (Jesus) is breaking the wisdom-stream's discriminating-bread-fellowship rule by eating with those Sirach 12 instructed his disciples to hold-back-from. The framework reading: not every wisdom-stream teaching is operative in the kingdom-at-hand; the King's direct-mercy supersedes the wisdom-stream's categorical-exclusion stance.
new_note: *Do well to him that is lowly, but give not to the ungodly: hold back your bread, and give it not to him, lest he overmaster you thereby: for else you shall receive twice as much evil for all the good you shall have done to him.* (Ecclesiasticus 12:5). *And when the Pharisees saw it, they said unto his disciples, Why eateth your Master with publicans and sinners?* (Matthew 9:11). Sirach says to do well to the lowly but to hold back your bread from the ungodly, because what you give him he will turn into power over you. The Pharisees asked why the Master ate with publicans and sinners, as if this verse had been broken. It had not. Sirach is warning against strengthening a man in his wickedness; Yahusha (Jesus) was eating with men who had come to hear him and were being called out of theirs. The ungodly in Sirach is the man who stays ungodly with your bread in his hand; the sinner at the King's table is the one who heard and sat down.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 12:5 — *hold back your bread, and give it not to him, lest he overmaster you thereby.* Bread held back from the one who would overmaster you is not the table the Pharisees question at Matthew 9:11.

apoc_text: Give to the good, and help not the sinner.
old_note: *Give to the good, and help not the sinner.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 12:7 reiterates the wisdom-stream's categorical-exclusion stance the King reverses at Matt 9:13. Yahusha (Jesus) is *not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance* — the inverse of the Sirach 12 mandate. The wisdom-stream had a wrong-stance on this; the King restores the heart-Torah by going TO the sinners precisely because the wisdom-stream's discriminating-mercy excluded them. The Hosea 6:6 mercy-substance is BROADER than the wisdom-stream's godly-righteous register; it extends to the sinners-to-be-called.
new_note: *Give to the good, and help not the sinner.* (Ecclesiasticus 12:7). *But go ye and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.* (Matthew 9:13). Sirach says it again: give to the good, help not the sinner. Yahusha (Jesus) says he came not to call the righteous but sinners to repentance, and he sends the Pharisees to learn what mercy and not sacrifice means. The two verses meet at the word repentance. Sirach withholds help from the sinner who stays a sinner; the King calls the sinner to stop being one, and the mercy he names is the call itself. Neither verse feeds a man in his wickedness, and neither shuts the door on the man who turns.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 12:7 — *Give to the good, and help not the sinner.* Help not the sinner and call sinners to repentance (Matthew 9:13) meet at the word repentance.

apoc_text: Prayer is good with fasting and alms and righteousness. A little with righteousness is better than much with unrighteousness. It is better to give alms than to lay up gold:
old_note: *Prayer is good with fasting and alms and righteousness. A little with righteousness is better than much with unrighteousness. It is better to give alms than to lay up gold.* Tobit 12:8 (the angel Raphael's instruction) names the wisdom-stream's prayer-fasting-alms-righteousness triad as the operative-discipline of the godly. Matt 9:14's fasting-question presupposes the Pharisaic-style fasting-as-credential-without-the-mercy-triad operative; Yahusha (Jesus) does not abolish fasting (he affirms it at v.15b *then shall they fast*) but reframes it in the bridegroom-architecture and in the Tobit-mercy-triad. Fasting alone is not the discipline; fasting WITH prayer, alms, and righteousness is the wisdom-stream's teaching the King restores.
new_note: *Prayer is good with fasting and alms and righteousness. A little with righteousness is better than much with unrighteousness. It is better to give alms than to lay up gold:* (Tobit 12:8). *Then came to him the disciples of John, saying, Why do we and the Pharisees fast oft, but thy disciples fast not?* (Matthew 9:14). The angel Raphael tells Tobit and his son that prayer is good with fasting and alms and righteousness, all together, and that a little with righteousness outweighs much without it. John's disciples asked Yahusha (Jesus) why his disciples did not fast as they and the Pharisees did. He does not throw fasting out — he says the days will come when they will fast (9:15) — but he sets it where the angel set it, as one part of a life of mercy and righteousness, not a credential by itself. Fasting alone was never the discipline; fasting with prayer, alms, and righteousness is what the library taught and what the King restores.
member_note: Tobit 12:8 — *Prayer is good with fasting and alms and righteousness.* Fasting belongs with prayer, alms, and righteousness, not alone; the King keeps it in that place (Matthew 9:14).

apoc_text: So is it with a man that fasteth for his sins, and goes again, and doeth the same: who will hear his prayer? or what does his humbling profit him?
old_note: *So is it with a man that fasteth for his sins, and goes again, and doeth the same: who will hear his prayer? or what does his humbling profit him?* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 34:26 names the wisdom-stream's fasting-without-repentance-is-vain diagnostic explicitly — the faster who fasts for his sins and continues in them is not heard. The Pharisaic-counterfeit form at Matt 9:14 is fasting-as-credential while the categorical-exclusion-of-sinners and the mercy-withholding continues; Sirach 34:26 had named the diagnostic centuries before. The King's bridegroom-frame at Matt 9:15 reframes fasting in the wedding-substance; the post-ascension assembly fasts (*then shall they fast*) but in the mercy-substance Sirach 34:26 implied as the precondition.
new_note: *So is it with a man that fasteth for his sins, and goes again, and doeth the same: who will hear his prayer? or what does his humbling profit him?* (Ecclesiasticus 34:26). *And Yahusha (Jesus) said unto them, Can the children of the bridechamber mourn, as long as the bridegroom is with them? but the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken from them, and then shall they fast.* (Matthew 9:15). Sirach asks what a man's fast profits him when he fasts for his sins and then goes back and does the same; who will hear his prayer? When John's disciples asked why his disciples did not fast, Yahusha (Jesus) did not do away with fasting; he said the days would come when they would fast. But he placed it after the bridegroom is taken, in the grief of a people who have truly lost something, not as a routine kept while nothing changes. Sirach had already named the difference: a fast that turns from the sin is heard, and a fast that returns to it is noise.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 34:26 — *a man that fasteth for his sins, and goes again, and doeth the same: who will hear his prayer?.* Fasting that turns is heard; *then shall they fast* (Matthew 9:15) is fasting with the loss truly felt.

apoc_text: Forsake not an old friend; for the new is not comparable to him: a new friend is as new wine; when it is old, you shall drink it with pleasure.
old_note: *Forsake not an old friend; for the new is not comparable to him: a new friend is as new wine; when it is old, you shall drink it with pleasure.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 9:10 names the wisdom-stream's old-vs-new wine register — the wisdom-stream holds the old friend (and the old wine) as more trustworthy than the new. The framework reads Matt 9:17's new-wine / new-bottles parable in inverse register: the wisdom-stream's old-is-better register is precisely the Pharisaic-rabbinic-system's self-justification — the old-tradition-fences cannot be ruptured by the new heart-Torah-walking. The framework angle is that the wisdom-stream RECOGNIZES the new-vs-old containment question as a real question; the gospel REFRAMES it by naming the heart-Torah-substance the new-heart container holds and the Pharisaic-old-bottle cannot. The Torah itself is NEITHER the wine NOR the wineskin; the Pharisaic-system's wisdom-stream-old-friend-loyalty is the old wineskin that bursts when the heart-Torah-life enters.
new_note: *Forsake not an old friend; for the new is not comparable to him: a new friend is as new wine; when it is old, you shall drink it with pleasure.* (Ecclesiasticus 9:10). *Neither do men put new wine into old bottles: else the bottles break, and the wine runneth out, and the bottles perish: but they put new wine into new bottles, and both are preserved.* (Matthew 9:17). Sirach honors the old friend and the old wine; the new has to age before it is worth drinking. Yahusha (Jesus) is not quarreling with that. The question put to him in Matthew 9 was about fasting, and his answer is about the vessel: new wine poured into a brittle old skin bursts it and both are lost. The Torah is neither the wine nor the skin; it is the vineyard the wine comes from. The skin that cannot stretch is the body of added tradition, and the wine the King pours will itself grow old and be drunk with pleasure, exactly as Sirach says new wine does.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 9:10 — *a new friend is as new wine; when it is old, you shall drink it with pleasure.* Sirach's new wine that ages well sits beside the new wine and new bottles of Matthew 9:17.
writer_flag: Theology correction: the old note read Sirach's old-friend loyalty as itself the Pharisaic old wineskin that bursts — pitting the wisdom book against the gospel. Rewritten so the two agree: the Torah is neither wine nor skin, the brittle skin is added tradition, and Sirach's own line (new wine ages into pleasure) supports rather than opposes the King.

apoc_text: My son, in your sickness be not negligent: but pray to Yahuah (God), and he will make you whole.
old_note: *My son, in your sickness be not negligent: but pray to Yahuah (God), and he will make you whole.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 38:9 names the wisdom-stream's prescribed-healing-architecture: pray to the Most High first; he will make you whole. The bleeding-woman of Matt 9:20-22 walks an inversion of the Sirach-38 architecture in one register and a fulfillment in another. The framework reads the inversion: she does not pray-then-wait for the indirect-healing-flow Sirach prescribes; she touches the King's garment directly because the King is the Formed-Voice through whom the Most High's healing-flow operates in present-tense-direct.
new_note: *My son, in your sickness be not negligent: but pray to Yahuah (God), and he will make you whole.* (Ecclesiasticus 38:9). *And, behold, a woman, which was diseased with an issue of blood twelve years, came behind him, and touched the hem of his garment:* (Matthew 9:20). Sirach tells the sick man not to be negligent but to pray to Yahuah (God), who will make him whole. The woman with the issue of blood had been sick twelve years, and she came behind Yahusha (Jesus) and touched the hem of his garment, and he turned and told her that her faith had made her whole. She was not going around Sirach's counsel; she was doing it. The one who spoke and walked with the fathers was standing in the crowd in flesh, and reaching for his garment was her prayer to Yahuah (God).
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 38:9 — *pray to Yahuah (God), and he will make you whole.* The woman who touched the hem (Matthew 9:20) made that prayer with her hand.
writer_flag: Theology correction: the old note called the woman's touch an 'inversion' or 'bypass' of Sirach's pray-first counsel. Rewritten: Yahusha (Jesus) is the Formed one who spoke in the Tanakh, so reaching for him is the prayer Sirach prescribes, not a way around it.

apoc_text: Then give place to the physician, for Yahuah (God) has created him: let him not go from you, for you have need of him.
old_note: *Then give place to the physician, for Yahuah (God) has created him: let him not go from you, for you have need of him.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 38:12 names the wisdom-stream's give-place-to-the-physician prescription. The bleeding-woman of Matt 9:20-22 had given place to physicians for twelve years (Mark 5:26 records the Sirach-38 prescription faithfully followed and failed); the King's direct-cleansing-source-touch reverses the defiling-flow that the physician-chain could not heal — and Yahusha (Jesus) names her faith (not her physician-adherence) as the architecture of her wholeness at v.22.
new_note: *Then give place to the physician, for Yahuah (God) has created him: let him not go from you, for you have need of him.* (Ecclesiasticus 38:12). *But Yahusha (Jesus) turned him about, and when he saw her, he said, Daughter, be of good comfort; thy faith hath made thee whole. And the woman was made whole from that hour.* (Matthew 9:22). Sirach does not slight the physician; he says Yahuah (God) created him and tells the sick man to keep him close. The woman with the issue of blood did exactly that for twelve years, and Mark 5:26 adds that she spent all she had on physicians and only grew worse. When she reached for the hem of his garment she was reaching past the physician to the one who made the physician, and Yahusha (Jesus) does not rebuke the years she spent under their care; he names her faith as what made her whole. The physician is a gift from his hand, and the healing was always his.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 38:12 — *give place to the physician, for Yahuah (God) has created him.* The bleeding woman gave place to physicians for twelve years; at Matthew 9:22 she reached past them to the one who made them, and her faith made her whole.

apoc_text: For they shall also pray to Yahuah (God), that he would prosper that, which they give for ease and remedy to prolong life.
old_note: *For they shall also pray to Yahuah (God), that he would prosper that, which they give for ease and remedy to prolong life.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 38:14 names the wisdom-stream's physician-prays-to-the-Most-High architecture — the physician's success is itself dependent on the Most High's prosper-the-remedy authority. At Matt 9:25 the King takes the dead girl's hand directly; the physician-chain has reached its limit (the girl is dead), and the prosper-the-remedy authority Sirach 38 names as flowing through the physician-prayer-chain is now exercised directly by the Formed-in-flesh.
new_note: *For they shall also pray to Yahuah (God), that he would prosper that, which they give for ease and remedy to prolong life.* (Ecclesiasticus 38:14). *But when the people were put forth, he went in, and took her by the hand, and the maid arose.* (Matthew 9:25). Sirach says the physician himself prays to Yahuah (God) that the remedy in his hand would prosper, because the healing never belonged to the remedy. In the ruler's house the remedies have run out; the girl is dead, and no physician prays over a corpse. Yahusha (Jesus) walks in and takes her by the hand, and the one the physician prays to is the one standing in the room. The physician asks for the prospering; here the giver of it does the work with his own hand.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 38:14 — *they shall also pray to Yahuah (God), that he would prosper that, which they give.* The physician prays that his remedy would prosper; at Matthew 9:25 the one he prays to takes the dead girl by the hand himself.

apoc_text: For you have power of life and death: you leadest to the gates of hell, and bringest up again.
old_note: *For you have power of life and death: you leadest to the gates of hell, and bringest up again.* Wisdom of Solomon 16:13 names the wisdom-stream's direct architecture of the Most High's power-of-life-and-death: he leads to the gates of hell, and brings up again. Matt 9:24's *the maid is not dead, but sleepeth* and 9:25's raising-of-Yair's-daughter walk the same architecture in flesh-presence: the King who exercises the power-of-life-and-death IS the Formed through whom that power operates. The wisdom-stream had named the Most High's authority over death; the King at Matt 9:25 IS that authority in flesh.
new_note: *For you have power of life and death: you leadest to the gates of hell, and bringest up again.* (Wisdom of Solomon 16:13). *He said unto them, Give place: for the maid is not dead, but sleepeth. And they laughed him to scorn.* (Matthew 9:24). Power of life and death belongs to Yahuah (God): he leads to the gates of hell, the grave, and brings up again. In the ruler's house the King looked at a dead girl and said she was not dead but sleeping, and the mourners laughed at him. Then he took her by the hand and she arose. The one who brings up again from the gates of the grave was standing in the room in flesh, and death in his presence is sleep because he is the one who wakes it. The righteous dead are asleep the same way, and the hand that took the girl's hand is the one that will bring them up.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 16:13 — *you have power of life and death: you leadest to the gates of hell, and bringest up again.* The maid not dead but sleeping (Matthew 9:24) is raised by the one who leads to the grave and brings up again.

apoc_text: A man indeed killeth through his malice: and the spirit, when it is gone forth, returns not; neither the soul received up comes again.
old_note: *A man indeed killeth through his malice: and the spirit, when it is gone forth, returns not; neither the soul received up comes again.* Wisdom of Solomon 16:14 names the wisdom-stream's mortal-man-cannot-bring-back diagnostic explicitly — the spirit that is gone returns not; the soul received up comes not again BY MAN. The framework reads Matt 9:25 against the diagnostic: the King brings back the spirit that has gone, raises the daughter the wisdom-stream had named no-mortal-can-raise. The Formed-in-flesh exercises the prerogative the wisdom-stream had named as the Most High's alone — confirming the Formed-from-the-Formless framework on the nature of Yahusha (Jesus).
new_note: *A man indeed killeth through his malice: and the spirit, when it is gone forth, returns not; neither the soul received up comes again.* (Wisdom of Solomon 16:14). *But when the people were put forth, he went in, and took her by the hand, and the maid arose.* (Matthew 9:25). The verse draws the line a man cannot cross: he can kill, but once the spirit has gone forth he cannot call it back. Then Yahusha (Jesus) takes a dead girl by the hand and she arises. What Wisdom of Solomon had just said belongs to Yahuah (God) alone — the power of life and death, leading down and bringing up again (16:13) — is done in a house in Capernaum by a man with his hand on a child. That is who he is: not the formless Father, but the one through whom the Father's power has always acted, now standing in flesh.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 16:14 — *the spirit, when it is gone forth, returns not.* What no man can do, the King does with his hand on a dead girl (Matthew 9:25).

apoc_text: And the lion, whom you sawest rising up out of the wood, and roaring, and speaking to the eagle, and rebuking her for her unrighteousness with all the words which you have heard;
old_note: *And the lion, whom you sawest rising up out of the wood, and roaring, and speaking to the eagle, and rebuking her for her unrighteousness with all the words which you have heard...* 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 12:31 names the lion-rising-out-of-the-wood vision the Most High's angel-interpreter identifies as the Messiah-from-the-seed-of-David at v.32. The framework reads the lion-symbol as the wisdom-stream's apocalyptic-register naming of the Davidic-Messianic restoration-figure — the lion who rebukes the eagle (the fourth-beast-empire of Daniel 7) is the Messiah-anointed who Matt 9:27's blind men confess as *Son of David.*
new_note: *And the lion, whom you sawest rising up out of the wood, and roaring, and speaking to the eagle, and rebuking her for her unrighteousness with all the words which you have heard; This is the anointed, which the Highest has kept for them and for their wickedness to the end: he shall reprove them, and shall upbraid them with their cruelty.* (2 Esdras 12:31–32). *And when Yahusha (Jesus) departed thence, two blind men followed him, crying, and saying, Thou Son of David, have mercy on us.* (Matthew 9:27). Ezra's lion comes up roaring out of the wood and rebukes the eagle, which he had been told is the fourth kingdom Daniel saw (2 Esdras 12:11), and the angel then names the lion: the anointed, kept by the Highest to the end. Two blind men on the road name the same figure by his line, Son of David. The anointed one Ezra saw as a lion, the blind men perceived with no eyes, and they cried out to him as present. The Messiah (Christ) kept for the end was walking past them.
member_note: 2 Esdras 12:31 — *the lion, whom you sawest rising up out of the wood, and roaring.* The lion named as the anointed is the Son of David the blind men cry to at Matthew 9:27.

apoc_text: This is the anointed, which the Highest has kept for them and for their wickedness to the end: he shall reprove them, and shall upbraid them with their cruelty.
old_note: *This is the anointed, which the Highest has kept for them and for their wickedness to the end: he shall reprove them, and shall upbraid them with their cruelty.* 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 12:32 names the lion-figure as the anointed (the Messiah / Christ) the Most High has kept against the end-of-the-age — the figure who shall reprove and upbraid the cruelty of the wicked. The framework's Davidic-Messianic register at Matt 9:27 has its wisdom-stream apocalyptic-witness here: the Messiah-anointed from-the-seed-of-David is the figure the blind men confess in present-tense, and the figure 2 Esdras names as kept for the end. The same figure; the apocalyptic-stream named him; the in-flesh-King walks him.
new_note: *This is the anointed, which the Highest has kept for them and for their wickedness to the end: he shall reprove them, and shall upbraid them with their cruelty.* (2 Esdras 12:32). *And when Yahusha (Jesus) departed thence, two blind men followed him, crying, and saying, Thou Son of David, have mercy on us.* (Matthew 9:27). The angel tells Ezra what the lion is: the anointed, kept by the Highest to the end, who will reprove the wicked for their cruelty. Two blind men cry to Yahusha (Jesus) as Son of David, the line the anointed king comes from. The one kept to the end to reprove the proud is the one who stops in the road for the blind who ask for mercy. The same anointed, seen by Ezra in a vision and met on a road.
member_note: 2 Esdras 12:32 — *This is the anointed, which the Highest has kept for them.* The anointed kept to the end is the Son of David met on the road at Matthew 9:27.

apoc_text: For the rest of my people shall he deliver with mercy, those that have been pressed upon my borders, and he shall make them joyful until the coming of the day of judgment, of which I have spoken to you from the beginning.
old_note: *For the rest of my people shall he deliver with mercy, those that have been pressed upon my borders, and he shall make them joyful until the coming of the day of judgment.* 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 12:34 names the Davidic-Messiah's deliver-with-mercy architecture explicitly — the Messiah delivers the remnant of the people with mercy, those who have been pressed upon the borders (the scattered seed). The framework's gathering-thesis lands at full weight in this verse: the Messiah-from-the-seed-of-David delivers the scattered-and-pressed remnant with mercy — Hosea 6:6's mercy-substance + the gathering of Matt 9:36 + the Davidic-Messianic recognition of Matt 9:27 are one architecture.
new_note: *For the rest of my people shall he deliver with mercy, those that have been pressed upon my borders, and he shall make them joyful until the coming of the day of judgment, of which I have spoken to you from the beginning.* (2 Esdras 12:34). *And when Yahusha (Jesus) departed thence, two blind men followed him, crying, and saying, Thou Son of David, have mercy on us.* (Matthew 9:27). The King gives his disciples the way into that day: confess him before men now, and he will confess them before the Father then. The confession is made in the face of the same people doing the afflicting, and the boldness Solomon saw is the boldness of the one being named by the Son in front of the Father while those who despised him look on.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 5:1 — *the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him.* The one who confesses the King before his afflicters (Matthew 10:32) is the one who stands in boldness before them on that day.

new_note: *Then I answered and said, How, and when shall these things come to pass? wherefore are our years few and evil?* (2 Esdras 4:33). *And said unto him, Art thou he that should come, or do we look for another?* (Matthew 11:3). Esdras, shown the end and the threshing, asks the question anyone in distress asks: how, and when, and why are our years few and evil. John, in Herod's prison, sends to ask Yahusha (Jesus), art thou he that should come, or do we look for another. John had preached the axe at the root and the fan in the hand, and the fire had not fallen while he sat in chains. Neither question is unbelief. Both are the faithful asking the one who knows the times why the times are not yet what he said they would be.
member_note: 2 Esdras 4:33 — *How, and when shall these things come to pass? wherefore are our years few and evil?.* John's question from prison (Matthew 11:3) is the same question from the same distress.

apoc_text: And he answered me, saying, Do not you hasten above the most Highest: for your haste is in vain to be above him, for you have much exceeded.
old_note: *And he answered me, saying, Do not you hasten above the most Highest: for your haste is in vain to be above him, for you have much exceeded.* 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 4:34 names the wisdom-stream's direct angelic-answer to the prophet's timing-question: do not hasten above the Most High; the timing is his. Matt 11:6's *blessed is he, whosoever shall not be offended in me* names the same disposition at the kingdom-citizens level — the blessing on the one who holds the credential, trusts the timeline, and does not fall away in the gap between the inaugurated-and-not-yet-consummated. The wisdom-stream had named the disposition the angel commended; the King at Matt 11:6 names it at the apostolic-mission level.
new_note: *And he answered me, saying, Do not you hasten above the most Highest: for your haste is in vain to be above him, for you have much exceeded.* (2 Esdras 4:34). *And blessed is he, whosoever shall not be offended in me.* (Matthew 11:6). The angel's answer to Esdras is not a date; it is, do not hasten above the Most High, the times are his and your hurry cannot move them. The King's answer to John is not a date either; after naming the works being done he adds, blessed is he who is not offended in me. Both answers ask the same thing of the one waiting: that he not stumble over the gap between what was promised and what he can see from where he sits. The blessing is on the one who trusts the timing of Yahuah (God) when the timing is the hardest part.
member_note: 2 Esdras 4:34 — *Do not you hasten above the most Highest: for your haste is in vain to be above him.* Blessed is he who is not offended in the waiting (Matthew 11:6).

old_note: *Did not the souls also of the righteous ask question of these things in their chambers, saying, How long shall I hope on this fashion? when comes the fruit of the floor of our reward?* 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 4:35 names the wisdom-stream's direct architecture of the souls-of-the-righteous-in-their-chambers-asking-how-long. new_note: *Did not the souls also of the righteous ask question of these things in their chambers, saying, How long shall I hope on this fashion? when comes the fruit of the floor of our reward?* (2 Esdras 4:35). *And blessed is he, whosoever shall not be offended in me.* (Matthew 11:6). The righteous dead ask from their chambers how long they must hope this way. John saw the same souls under the altar asking how long, O Yahuah (Lord), and they were told to rest a little while longer (Revelation 6:9–11). The King's word to John the Baptist in his prison is the word for everyone who waits: blessed is he who is not offended in me. The dead wait in their chambers, the living wait in their chains, and the blessing is on both for not letting the length of the wait turn into offense at the one who set its length.
member_note: 2 Esdras 4:35 — *Did not the souls also of the righteous ask question of these things in their chambers.* The one who waits without being offended is blessed (Matthew 11:6).

apoc_text: Who were ordained for reproofs in their times, to pacify the wrath of the judgment of Yahuah (God), before it brake forth into fury, and to turn the heart of the father to the son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob.
old_note: *Who were ordained for reproofs in their times, to pacify the wrath of the judgment of Yahuah (God), before it brake forth into fury, and to turn the heart of the father to the son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 48:10 names THE strongest wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the Eliyahu-pattern: ordained-for-reproofs, pacify-the-wrath-of-judgment, turn-the-heart-of-the-father-to-the-son, AND *restore the tribes of Jacob* — the twelve-tribe-gathering substance the framework's Red Line #11 names as the destination of the gathering-of-the-scattered-seed. Matt 11:14's *if ye will receive it, this is Eliyahu (Elijah), which was for to come* identifies Yochanan (John) as the Eliyahu-pattern fulfillment; Sirach 48:10 names the same Eliyahu-pattern at the wisdom-stream register, with the *restore the tribes of Jacob* clause locking the twelve-tribe-restoration architecture as integral to the Eliyahu-mission. The framework reads Yochanan (John) as the inaugural-Eliyahu-pattern-fulfillment; the dreadful-day-of-Yahuah (the LORD) full-restoration-of-the-tribes-of-Jacob is reserved for the second-coming.
new_note: *Who were ordained for reproofs in their times, to pacify the wrath of the judgment of Yahuah (God), before it brake forth into fury, and to turn the heart of the father to the son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob.* (Ecclesiasticus 48:10). *And if ye will receive it, this is Elias, which was for to come.* (Matthew 11:14). When Yahusha (Jesus) says John is the Elias who was to come, he is pointing at a job description everyone in the crowd knew. Sirach had written it out: Elijah is ordained to reprove, to turn the heart of the father to the son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob. All of Jacob, all twelve tribes, the scattered house of Yashar'el (Israel) and the house of Yahudah (Judah) together. John began that work at the Jordan; the full restoring of the tribes waits on the great and dreadful day Malachi set it beside (Malachi 4:5). *If ye will receive it* is the hard part, because receiving it means receiving that the gathering of a scattered people is what Elijah comes to do.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 48:10 — *to restore the tribes of Jacob.* Yahusha (Jesus) names John as Elias at Matthew 11:14, and Sirach says what Elijah comes to do: restore the tribes of Jacob, all twelve.

apoc_text: Elias for being zealous and fervent for the law was taken up into heaven.
old_note: *Elias for being zealous and fervent for the law was taken up into heaven.* 1 Maccabees 2:58 names the wisdom-stream's witness to the Eliyahu-zealous-for-the-Torah architecture: Eliyahu's zeal for the Torah is what the wisdom-stream remembers as the operative-substance of his mission. Matt 11:14's Eliyahu-pattern-identification of Yochanan (John) walks the same architecture — Yochanan (John) was the wilderness-camel-hair Nazirite-disciplined prophet whose zeal for the Father's-ways called the Pharisees and Sadducees *generation of vipers* (Matt 3:7) and whose imprisonment came from his public-condemnation of Herod Antipas's adultery (Matt 14:3-4). The wisdom-stream had named the Eliyahu-zealous-for-Torah disposition; the inaugural-Eliyahu-fulfillment in Yochanan (John) walks the same disposition at the messenger-before-the-King's-face register.
new_note: *Elias for being zealous and fervent for the law was taken up into heaven.* (1 Maccabees 2:58). *And if ye will receive it, this is Elias, which was for to come.* (Matthew 11:14). Mattathias remembers Elijah (Elias) for one thing: he was zealous and fervent for the law, and he was taken up into heaven. That is how the faithful in Yashar'el (Israel) remembered him, as the man who stood for the commandments of Yahuah (God) against a kingdom that had traded them for Baal. When Yahusha (Jesus) says of John, this is Elijah (Elias) which was for to come, the likeness is that same zeal: John in the wilderness calling the leadership a generation of vipers, John in prison for telling Herod his marriage was unlawful. Elijah's zeal for the law is what Malachi promised would come before the great day, and it came first in John.
member_note: 1 Maccabees 2:58 — *Elias for being zealous and fervent for the law was taken up into heaven.* John came in that same zeal; this is Elias which was for to come (Matthew 11:14).

apoc_text: Therefore let us lie in wait for the righteous; because he is not for our turn, and he is clean contrary to our doings: he upbraideth us with our offending the law, and objecteth to our infamy the transgressings of our education.
old_note: *Therefore let us lie in wait for the righteous; because he is not for our turn, and he is clean contrary to our doings: he upbraideth us with our offending the law, and objecteth to our infamy the transgressings of our education.* Wisdom of Solomon 2:12 names the wisdom-stream's direct prophecy of the system's-rejection-of-the-righteous-one architecture: let-us-lie-in-wait, because-he-upbraids-us-with-our-offending-the-law. The framework reads the verse as the prophetic-pre-figuration of the Pharisaic-system's rejection of both Yochanan (John) and Yahusha (Jesus) at Matt 11:18-19. The system's opposite-direction-complaints (Yochanan-too-austere; Yahusha-friend-of-publicans) are cover-stories over the prior decision Wisdom 2 had named in advance — the righteous-one who reproves with the Torah is intolerable to a system invested in its own departure from it.
new_note: *Therefore let us lie in wait for the righteous; because he is not for our turn, and he is clean contrary to our doings: he upbraideth us with our offending the law, and objecteth to our infamy the transgressings of our education.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:12). *The Son of Adam came eating and drinking, and they say, Behold a man gluttonous, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners. But wisdom is justified of her children.* (Matthew 11:19). The system faulted John for fasting and Yahusha (Jesus) for eating, which tells you the complaints were not the reason. Wisdom of Solomon gave the reason long before: the righteous one is clean contrary to our doings and upbraids us with our offending the law, so let us lie in wait for him. The glutton and winebibber charge is a cover for the grievance the ungodly admit among themselves, that his life exposes their departure from the Torah. *Wisdom is justified of her children* because wisdom's own book had already written the accusers' script.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:12 — *he is clean contrary to our doings: he upbraideth us with our offending the law.* The contradictory complaints of Matthew 11:19 hide the real grievance Wisdom 2:12 names: the righteous one reproves their lawbreaking.

apoc_text: He is grievous to us even to behold: for his life is not like other men’s, his ways are of another fashion.
old_note: *He is grievous to us even to behold: for his life is not like other men's, his ways are of another fashion.* Wisdom of Solomon 2:15 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the system's-aesthetic-rejection of the righteous-one: his-life-is-not-like-other-men's, his-ways-of-another-fashion. The framework reads the verse as the wisdom-stream pre-figuration of the *gluttonous-man, winebibber, friend-of-publicans-and-sinners* slander at Matt 11:19 — the system's moral-character-attack on the King for the table-fellowship-with-sinners (Matt 9:10-13) is the operative-form of the system's-aesthetic-rejection Wisdom 2:15 had named. The system's register-of-rejection changes; the architecture does not.
new_note: *He is grievous to us even to behold: for his life is not like other men’s, his ways are of another fashion.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:15). *The Son of Adam came eating and drinking, and they say, Behold a man gluttonous, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners. But wisdom is justified of her children.* (Matthew 11:19). The ungodly in Wisdom cannot even stand to look at the righteous man, because his life is cut to another pattern than theirs. That is the complaint behind the slander in Matthew: the Son of Adam sat at table with publicans and sinners, and the religious system of his day could only read a life of another fashion as gluttony and drunkenness. The charge changes its words from one age to the next, but it is the same offense — a righteous life reproves the ones watching it, and they answer by calling it unrighteous. Wisdom is justified of her children all the same.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:15 — *his life is not like other men’s, his ways are of another fashion.* The life of another fashion is what the slander of Matthew 11:19 was aimed at — a glutton and winebibber for sitting with sinners.

apoc_text: Let us condemn him with a shameful death: for by his own saying he shall be respected.
old_note: *Let us condemn him with a shameful death: for by his own saying he shall be respected.* Wisdom of Solomon 2:20 names the wisdom-stream's direct prophecy of the system's-condemnation-of-the-righteous-one to a shameful death — the verbal-anchor for the trajectory the Matt 11:19 slander-escalation points toward (the Matt 12:24 Beelzebul-attribution, the Matt 26-27 cross-trial-and-execution). Matt 11:19's slander is the inaugural-form of the architecture Wisdom 2:20 had named at its full terminus: the system that cannot deny the visible-fact moves through slander, moves through false-attribution, moves toward condemnation to a shameful death. The wisdom-stream had named the full architecture; Matt 11:19 names the early-step.
new_note: *Let us condemn him with a shameful death: for by his own saying he shall be respected.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:20). *The Son of Adam came eating and drinking, and they say, Behold a man gluttonous, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners. But wisdom is justified of her children.* (Matthew 11:19). The ungodly in Wisdom finish where they were always headed: condemn him to a shameful death. In Matthew 11 they are only at the beginning — calling him a glutton and a winebibber for sitting with sinners. The road runs from there to Matthew 12, where his works are credited to Beelzebub, and on to the trial and the cross in Matthew 26 and 27. A system that cannot deny what it sees moves from slander to false accusation to execution. Wisdom had named the end of that road before the gospel showed its first step.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:20 — *Let us condemn him with a shameful death: for by his own saying he shall be respected.* The end of the road whose first step is the slander of Matthew 11:19.

Matt 11:19's *wisdom is justified of her children* closing (the inverse-of-the-system's-rejection naming the kingdom-citizens-whose-ears-the-Father-has-opened-recognize-the-substance) walks the same wisdom-personification-tradition. new_note: *Come to me, all you that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.* (Ecclesiasticus 24:19). *The Son of Adam came eating and drinking, and they say, Behold a man gluttonous, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners. But wisdom is justified of her children.* (Matthew 11:19). Wisdom calls out: come to me, all you who desire me, and fill yourselves with my fruits. Yahusha (Jesus) came eating and drinking, and the ones who came to him were the publicans and the sinners, while the system called him a glutton and a winebibber — and then he says wisdom is justified of her children. The children of wisdom are the ones who heard the call and came to be filled. The invitation Sirach wrote down is the one the Son of Adam spoke in Galilee, and his table was where the filling happened.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 24:19 — *Come to me, all you that be desirous of me.* Wisdom's invitation; *wisdom is justified of her children* who came (Matthew 11:19).

apoc_text: He has found out all the way of knowledge, and has given it to Jacob his servant, and to Yashar'el (Israel) his beloved.
old_note: *He has found out all the way of knowledge, and has given it to Jacob his servant, and to Yashar'el (Israel) his beloved.* Baruch 3:36 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the wisdom-given-to-Yashar'el (Israel) architecture: Yahuah (God) found-out the way of knowledge and gave it to Ya'aqov (Jacob) his servant and to Yashar'el (Israel) his beloved. The framework reads the verse against Red Line #11's scattered-seed-covenant-substance: the wisdom-given is given to the covenant-seed; the wisdom-children at Matt 11:19 are the kingdom-citizens-whose-ears-the-Father-has-opened — the covenant-seed responding to the wisdom-given. Matt 11:19's wisdom-justified-of-her-children walks the same architecture: the wisdom-given to Ya'aqov (Jacob)-and-Yashar'el (Israel) at Baruch 3:36 is the substance the kingdom-citizens-of-wisdom recognize.
new_note: *He has found out all the way of knowledge, and has given it to Jacob his servant, and to Yashar'el (Israel) his beloved.* (Baruch 3:36). *The Son of Adam came eating and drinking, and they say, Behold a man gluttonous, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners. But wisdom is justified of her children.* (Matthew 11:19). Baruch says the whole way of knowledge was found out by Elohim (God) and then given, not to the world at large but to Jacob his servant and to Yashar'el (Israel) his beloved. Wisdom has a people she was given to. Yahusha (Jesus), reproached for eating with publicans and sinners, says wisdom is justified of her children: the ones who recognize her are her own. The children of wisdom in Matthew 11 are the covenant seed Baruch names, the people the knowledge was given to, and when wisdom walked among them in flesh they knew her voice even when the leaders did not. Her children are the proof she was given to Jacob.
member_note: Baruch 3:36 — *has given it to Jacob his servant, and to Yashar'el (Israel) his beloved.* Wisdom's children at Matthew 11:19 are the people she was given to.

apoc_text: This is the book of the commandments of Yahuah (God), and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.
old_note: *This is the book of the commandments of Yahuah (God), and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.* Baruch 4:1 names the wisdom-stream's direct identification of the wisdom-given-to-Yashar'el (Israel) as *the book of the commandments of Yahuah (God), and the law that endureth for ever.* The framework reads the verse as a load-bearing wisdom-stream anchor against the institutional-Christian antinomian-reading of the New Testament: the wisdom-given is the Torah; the Torah endures forever; those who keep it come to life; those who leave it die. Matt 11:19's *wisdom is justified of her children* names the kingdom-citizens-who-keep-the-commandments-of-Yahuah (God) — the same body the 1 John 2:3-4 *keep-his-commandments-or-the-truth-is-not-in-him* filter identifies.
new_note: *This is the book of the commandments of Yahuah (God), and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.* (Baruch 4:1). *The Son of Adam came eating and drinking, and they say, Behold a man gluttonous, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners. But wisdom is justified of her children.* (Matthew 11:19). Baruch names what the wisdom given to Jacob is: the book of the commandments of Yahuah (God), the law that endures for ever, which gives life to those who keep it and death to those who leave it. Wisdom is not a mood or a philosophy; she is the Torah. So when Yahusha (Jesus) says wisdom is justified of her children, her children are the ones who keep the commandments. John says the same thing from the other side: *He that saith, I know him, and keepeth not his commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in him* (1 John 2:4). The law that endureth for ever has not been set aside by the one who is Wisdom herself; her children are known by keeping it.
member_note: Baruch 4:1 — *the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life.* Wisdom is the Torah; her children keep it (Matthew 11:19).

apoc_text: Horribly and speedily shall he come upon you: for a sharp judgment shall be to them that be in high places.
old_note: *Horribly and speedily shall he come upon you: for a sharp judgment shall be to them that be in high places.* Wisdom of Solomon 6:5 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the graduated-judgment-of-the-credentialed: a sharp judgment to those in high places. Matt 11:21-22's *more tolerable for Tyre and Tsidon (Sidon) at the day of judgment, than for you* names the same graduated-judgment-architecture at the cities-that-saw-the-credential register. The wisdom-stream had named the principle: position-of-credential-or-authority brings sharper-judgment than position-without. The King at Matt 11:21-22 names the operative-application: the Galilean-cities-of-the-credentialing bear sharper-judgment than Tyre and Tsidon (Sidon) of the prophetic-indictments.
new_note: *Horribly and speedily shall he come upon you: for a sharp judgment shall be to them that be in high places.* (Wisdom of Solomon 6:5). *Woe unto thee, Chorazin! woe unto thee, Bethsaida! for if the mighty works, which were done in you, had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.* (Matthew 11:21). A sharp judgment belongs to those in high places. Chorazin and Bethsaida were set in a high place: the mighty works were done in their streets, and they did not repent. Tyre and Sidon, cities the prophets thundered against, would have been in sackcloth long ago if they had seen the same works. The more that is shown to a city or a man, the sharper the reckoning, and Solomon had written that rule before the King applied it to the towns he had been healing in.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 6:5 — *a sharp judgment shall be to them that be in high places.* Chorazin and Bethsaida (Matthew 11:21) saw the mighty works and did not repent; the more shown, the sharper the judgment.
